source.title: Think Through a Bottleneck: Hourglass Reasoning for Rigorous Induction

confidence_rationale: Mapping fidelity is the highest in this pull -- the paper implements and then ABLATES stage isolation in an induction pipeline, which is ARC-113's non-collapse requirement stated as an engineering manipulation. The Struct-SR ablation (structured intermediates WITHOUT isolation collapsing below baseline) is the single most on-target result available anywhere in this search. Confidence is held below 0.75 by source quality: a single-author, non-peer-reviewed 2026 preprint on two proprietary model families, with a public ARC-AGI-2 evaluation set and an acknowledged optimistic bias in pass@5.
failure_signatures: On BBEH-Linguini with GPT-5.5 the staged architecture performed WORSE than the monolithic baseline (pass@1 58.3% -> 46.5%, pass@5 67.4% -> 63.1%), so enforced stage separation is not universally beneficial and can cost accuracy in some rule-induction domains.

Weak initial induction degraded final performance by 20.5 percentage points and the downstream Refiner could not compensate, showing that an ordered pipeline inherits a hard dependency on early-stage quality -- a characteristic failure signature of ORDERING, not merely of separation.

Structured intermediate representations WITHOUT enforced context isolation (the Struct-SR variant) collapsed accuracy below even the unstructured baseline, so naming the stages is insufficient; only the topology of information flow produced the gain.
Separation is enforced by prompting and context isolation rather than architectural constraint, so the paper offers no guarantee that the stages did not silently recombine inside the frozen model.

mapping.source_claim_statement: What actually matters is a structurally enforced isolation between reasoning stages, so that information can only pass between them as a compressed symbolic state; ablations confirm that the gains come from the isolation between stages and the quality of the initial induction, not from prompt wording or the particular symbolic form used.
mapping.ree_translation: A rule-induction system that separates induction, deduction, implementation and error-driven refinement into stages communicating only through a compressed rule state outperforms one in which those stages share a single undifferentiated context -- and REMOVING the isolation while keeping the stage vocabulary degrades performance below baseline. This is ARC-113's non-collapse requirement tested as a manipulation: collapsing the pipeline into one reasoning context produces a characteristic failure in which the system abandons the induced rule and patches the artifact directly, anchoring on instance-specific detail instead of the abstract regularity.
mapping.mapping_caveat: The stages here are prompt-level roles imposed on a FROZEN large language model, not learned components of a substrate; nothing is trained, and the isolation is soft (context partitioning) rather than architectural. REE's stages are substrate components with their own learning dynamics, so a gain from prompt-level isolation in an LLM is at best an existence proof that stage collapse has a measurable cost, not evidence about REE's substrate. The four Hourglass stages also map onto only the middle of ARC-113's cycle -- there is no analog of experience, behavioural interaction, or long-term integration.
mapping.source_context: Frozen GPT-5.5 and Gemini 3.1 Pro; three benchmarks -- ARC-AGI-2 (visual abstraction), ChipBench (Verilog synthesis), BBEH-Linguini (textual rule induction from linguistics-olympiad puzzles).

confidence_components.notes: For an architectural claim mapping_fidelity is weighted heaviest, which is what lifts this entry above its modest source quality. Transfer risk is elevated: a frozen-LLM prompting result may not survive translation to a trained substrate at all.
